- **Discount rate:** CAPM at 13.2% base, derived in SECTION 11.5. A sensitivity table runs 8–13.2%.

**What Rambus sells (FY2025 mix, from company release):** Product revenue $347.8M (49%, +41% YoY — DDR5 server RCD chipsets, PMICs); Royalties $271.5M-equivalent (38%); Contract/other (13%). **Moat — strong but narrower than the historical royalty model:** The moat now rests on (a) dominant share (~45% per secondary sources [Estimate]) in DDR5 RCDs — the register/clock-driver that sits on every server DIMM, certified against each CPU platform, with long qualification cycles and switching costs; (b) an IP portfolio that still generates ~$70–75M/quarter licensing billings (Q2'26 guide $76–82M) at ~100% incremental margin; (c) an ~80% blended gross margin that proves pricing power. The moat is **durable** — AI servers need more, faster memory (DDR5→MRDIMM, HBM), and every generation re-qualifies Rambus parts. **But** the revenue center of gravity has shifted from royalty (100% margin, no inventory) to products (60–65% gross-margin target [Company]), which structurally lowers blended gross margin and adds inventory/supply-chain risk.

**Market position:** #1 in DDR5 RCD; the memory-interface chip market is effectively a duopoly (Rambus + Montage/Renesas ecosystem), which is a strong structural position. Customer concentration — five customers ≈ 70% of revenue [Estimate, secondary — unverified against filings] — is the main structural weakness.

**Industry demand:** AI/data-center memory content growth is the core secular driver; management frames the opportunity as "faster-than-market expansion" (Wells Fargo TMT summit, via brief [Estimate]). DDR5 is still ramping; supply-chain (back-end packaging) constraints persist into 2027 [Company commentary via brief].

**Quality score (my synthesis):** Moat 4/5; Industry position 4/5; Business model durability 4/5; Cyclicality/volatility 3/5 (chip content mix + memory cycle); Financial strength 5/5 (net cash, 45% FCF margin). **Net: a high-quality compounder with one real structural caveat — it is becoming a chip company at a royalty-company valuation.**
